evals.prompt: I tried to scan my repo and got "defender: command not found". Sort it out.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the CLI is missing and onboards it: resolves the bundled scripts/bootstrap.ps1 and runs the Install phase (then Verify, then InstallSkills).
expectations: The response routes a missing-binary error to onboarding the Defender for Cloud CLI rather than treating it as a generic shell error.
The response runs the bundled scripts/bootstrap.ps1 with the Install step (e.g. & $bootstrap -Step Install).
After installing, the response continues with the Verify step before declaring success.

evals.prompt: Install and set up the Defender for Cloud CLI on my machine.
evals.expected_output: Walks the Install phase then the Verify phase via bootstrap.ps1.
expectations: The response runs the bootstrap.ps1 Install step.
The response runs the bootstrap.ps1 Verify step after Install to confirm the binary is on PATH.
The response does not skip straight to authentication before the binary is installed and verified.

evals.prompt: Get the defender CLI working so the scan skills are available.
evals.expected_output: Reaches the InstallSkills phase, which installs the bundled Copilot skills via 'defender agent --install'.
expectations: The response runs the bootstrap.ps1 InstallSkills step.
The response explains that InstallSkills installs the bundled Copilot scan skills (e.g. via 'defender agent --install').
Install and Verify are completed before InstallSkills.

evals.prompt: Set up the defender CLI so I can run container image scans.
evals.expected_output: Selects Path A (legacy auth) for image scans: runs AuthLegacy and sets the GDN_MDC_CLI_* environment.
expectations: The response selects the legacy authentication path (Path A) because container image scans use legacy auth.
The response runs the bootstrap.ps1 AuthLegacy step.
The response references the GDN_MDC_CLI_* environment variables (e.g. GDN_MDC_CLI_CLIENT_ID / GDN_MDC_CLI_TENANT_ID) set by legacy auth.
The response does not use the ASPM auth-push (Path B) for an image scan.

evals.prompt: I want to view the latest AI scan results for this repo. Set up whatever auth is needed.
evals.expected_output: Selects Path B (ASPM auth-push) for AI-scan/latest-result: enumerates tenants then runs AuthAspm with the confirmed tenant.
expectations: The response selects the ASPM auth-push path (Path B) because AI-scan / latest-result flows require it.
The response enumerates tenants first via the bootstrap.ps1 ListTenants step.
The response runs the bootstrap.ps1 AuthAspm step with a confirmed tenant id.
The response does not use the legacy Path A (AuthLegacy / GDN_MDC_CLI_*) for an AI scan.

evals.prompt: Authenticate the defender CLI for ai-scan submission.
evals.expected_output: Path B enumerates tenants and has the user confirm which tenant is DfD-onboarded before running AuthAspm.
expectations: The response runs the bootstrap.ps1 ListTenants step before authenticating.
The response surfaces the available tenants and asks the user to confirm the correct tenant before running AuthAspm.
The response does not run AuthAspm with an unconfirmed or guessed tenant id.

evals.prompt: The Install step said InstallCli.ps1 is not validly signed by Microsoft. Should I keep going?
evals.expected_output: Treats a failed Authenticode check as a hard stop: instructs the user not to proceed and never suggests bypassing the signature gate.
expectations: The response tells the user to stop / not proceed because a failed Authenticode signature check is a hard stop.
The response does not suggest bypassing the signature check (e.g. -SkipPublisherCheck, ignoring the signature, or any workaround).
The response recommends only proceeding once a validly Microsoft-signed installer is available.

evals.prompt: defender --version already works. Just scan my repo for security issues.
evals.expected_output: Skips onboarding because the CLI is already installed and proceeds to scanning.
expectations: The response does not re-run onboarding or the bootstrap.ps1 Install step because the CLI is already present.
The response proceeds to scanning the repo (delegating to the scan skill) instead of re-installing the CLI.
